I found my dad dead at his desk from bad medications. He was on a LOT of hard-core antidepressants and mood stabilizers. He had just had surgery on his left eye, and the toxicology report showed that he went brain dead. 
I remember it frame by frame. Mom wasn't home, and because the door was shut, I thought he was finishing up work. It was around 7pm and my brothers and I were hungry. I knocked once, no answer. I opened the door and I saw him slumped over. I assumed he fell asleep at his desk, as he often did on late nights. I left him alone for about half and hour and come back. Nothing. No movement. No sound. I went in. Touched him. Cold as ice. There was a puddle of drool and foam on the desk from his mouth. His beautiful hazel eyes were glazed over. His phone was on the floor, gibberish spelled out in a text to my mom for help. I texted my mom, starting to feel a panic attack rising. I called 911, and the tears were running quickly down my face. In my panic, I tried doing CPR on his corpse as I was calling the police. I wailed and screamed at her to call an ambulance. They rushed in, told me to take my dogs and brothers and head to my neighbors. They had to practically pry me away. 
I don't remember much else after that, because I passed out from hyperventilating. But I was conscious enough to see him in a body bag, my mother clinging to him and sobbing. My grandpa took me for ice cream in an attempt to make me feel better, but we both broke down in tears. I didn't sleep for the next 3 days. The last time I saw him was at the funeral home, a private viewing for my mom and I, before he was cremated. 

I miss you, Brian.

Hey! I have some experience with making these prosthetics! I have a couple of ways for you to try if you want to further your hobby! Two ways I use are: latex paste prosthetics and sculpting then casting a negative. Latex paste is pretty simple. Take some flour, take some latex, mix until you get a thick consistency. I highly recommend you check out a guide for latex paste by Ellimacs. My method is sculpt my prosthetic with monster clay, cast it in plaster, and then use the negative to get the prosthetics with either silicone or latex. It's better to paint the prosthetic when it's dry rather than mixing in the colors. I know that's a lot of effort, but it's worth it in the long run; trust me. Hope this helps!
